pages.intro: Peter was a fisherman named Simon. One day Jesus called him to leave his nets and follow him. Jesus gave him a new name, Peter, which means "rock," and chose him to lead the Church. Peter was brave, but he also made big mistakes. Jesus forgave him and trusted him again. Catholics honor Peter as the first pope.
story_paragraphs: Peter's first name was Simon. He and his brother Andrew were fishermen on the Sea of Galilee.

One day, Jesus walked along the shore and saw the two brothers casting a net into the water. He said to them, "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men." At once they left their nets and followed him.
Jesus gave Simon a new name. He called him Cephas, a word that means "rock." In our language, that name is Peter.

Later, Jesus asked his disciples, "Who do you say that I am?" Simon Peter answered, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God." Jesus told him, "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." He also said, "I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven."
Peter loved Jesus, but he was not perfect. On the night Jesus was arrested, Peter was afraid. Three times, he said he did not even know Jesus.

After Jesus rose from the dead, he met his disciples by the sea and shared breakfast with them. Then he asked Peter three times, "Do you love me?" Each time Peter answered yes. Jesus told him, "Feed my sheep." Jesus was asking Peter to take care of his people.

On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples. Peter stood up and spoke boldly to the crowd about Jesus. About three thousand people were baptized that day. Later, when Peter was put in prison for his faith, an angel led him out.

According to tradition, Peter went to the city of Rome and led the Church there. Around the year 64, he was killed for his faith in Jesus. Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome is said to be built over his grave. Catholics honor Peter as the first pope.

pages.intro: Paul was first called Saul. He did not believe in Jesus, and he tried to stop the people who did. Then, on a road to the city of Damascus, Jesus spoke to him, and Saul's whole life changed. He became one of the greatest missionaries ever. He traveled from city to city telling people about Jesus, and his letters are part of the Bible.
story_paragraphs: Paul was born in a city called Tarsus, in the land that is now Turkey. His name at first was Saul. He was Jewish, and he studied hard to become a teacher of his faith. He earned his living by making tents.
Saul thought the followers of Jesus were wrong. He went looking for them so he could have them arrested.

One day, Saul was traveling to the city of Damascus to arrest Christians there. Suddenly a light from the sky flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice say, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?" Saul asked, "Who are you, sir?" The voice answered, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting."
When Saul stood up, he could not see. His companions led him by the hand into Damascus. For three days, he was blind, and he did not eat or drink.

Then the Lord sent a Christian named Ananias to him. Ananias laid his hands on Saul and called him "Saul, my brother." At once, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He was baptized. Right away, he began telling everyone that Jesus is the Son of God.

Saul became known as Paul. From the city of Antioch, he set out on long journeys to tell people about Jesus, especially people who were not Jewish. He started communities of Christians in many cities. When he could not be with them, he wrote them letters. Those letters are now part of the Bible.
Paul's work was hard and dangerous. In Jerusalem, a crowd turned against him, and he was arrested and kept in prison for two years.

Paul died in Rome around the year 67. Tradition says he was killed for his faith in Jesus. Near the end of his life, one of his letters says, "I have competed well; I have finished the race; I have kept the faith."

pages.intro: John the Baptist had one great job: to get people ready for Jesus. He lived in the desert, wore clothes made of camel's hair, and ate locusts and wild honey. Crowds came to hear him. He told them to be sorry for their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River. One day, Jesus himself came to be baptized by John.
story_paragraphs: John's parents were Zechariah and Elizabeth. They were good people, but they were old, and they had no children. Elizabeth was a relative of Mary, the Mother of Jesus.

One day, Zechariah was serving in the Temple when the angel Gabriel appeared to him. The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John."
Zechariah found this hard to believe. Because he doubted, he was not able to speak until the baby came.

When the baby was born, the neighbors wanted to name him Zechariah, after his father. But Elizabeth said, "No. He will be called John." Zechariah asked for a tablet and wrote, "John is his name." At once he could speak again, and he praised God.

When John grew up, he lived in the desert. He wore clothing made of camel's hair with a leather belt, and he ate locusts and wild honey. He told the people to be sorry for their sins and to change their lives. Crowds came to him, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
John knew he was not the Savior. He said, "One mightier than I is coming after me."

One day, Jesus came from Nazareth and was baptized by John in the Jordan. A voice came from the heavens: "You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased." Later, when John saw Jesus coming, he told the people, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world."

John always told the truth, even to powerful people. He told King Herod that it was wrong for him to take his brother's wife. Herod had John put in prison, and later he had him killed. John's friends came and laid his body in a tomb.

pages.intro: Mary Magdalene was one of the women who followed Jesus and helped him. She stayed near him even when he was dying on the cross. On Easter morning, she went to his tomb while it was still dark. There, the risen Jesus called her by name. Then he sent her to tell the apostles the best news ever: "I have seen the Lord."
story_paragraphs: Mary Magdalene's name tells us where she came from. She was from Magdala, a town on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. She is also called Mary of Magdala.
The Gospel of Luke tells us that Jesus healed Mary. She had suffered very much, and Jesus set her free. After that, she followed him.
Mary traveled with Jesus and the twelve apostles as he went from town to town preaching. She was one of a group of women who took care of them, using what they owned to pay for what was needed.
When Jesus was arrested and crucified, many of his friends ran away. Mary Magdalene did not. She stood by the cross with Mary, the Mother of Jesus.

Early on Sunday morning, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb. The body of Jesus was not there. She ran to tell Peter and another disciple. They came and looked, and then they went home.
But Mary stayed outside the tomb, crying. She saw two angels in white. Then she turned around and saw a man standing there. She thought he was the gardener.

The man said to her, "Mary!" At that moment, she knew him. It was Jesus, alive! She answered, "Rabbouni," which means "Teacher." Jesus sent her to tell his disciples. Mary went and said to them, "I have seen the Lord."
Because she was sent to bring the news of Easter to the apostles, Mary Magdalene has been called the "Apostle to the Apostles."

pages.subtitle: The great angel who defends God's people against evil.

quick_facts.label: Who

pages.intro: Saint Michael is not a person who once lived on earth. He is an angel, a spirit created by God. The Bible calls him a great prince and the guardian of God's people. In the last book of the Bible, Michael and his angels fight against the devil and win. His name asks a question: "Who is like God?" The answer is no one.
story_paragraphs: Most saints were people who lived on earth, loved God, and are now with him in heaven. Saint Michael is different. He is an angel. Angels are spirits created by God. They do not have bodies like ours, and they are not born and do not die. They serve God and bring his help to people.
The Bible gives the names of only three angels: Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael. They are called archangels.

Michael's name comes from the Hebrew language. It means "Who is like God?" No one is like God, and that is the point. The devil wanted to put himself in God's place. Michael's very name says that God alone is God.
In the Old Testament, the Book of Daniel calls Michael "the great prince, guardian of your people." God's people trusted that Michael was watching over them.

In the last book of the Bible, the Book of Revelation, Saint John describes a great battle. "Then war broke out in heaven; Michael and his angels battled against the dragon." The dragon is a name for the devil. The dragon and its angels fought back, but they did not win, and they were thrown out of heaven.

Because of this, Christians have always asked Saint Michael to protect them from evil. In pictures and statues, he is often shown as a strong angel in armor, holding a sword, with the dragon under his feet.
Many people pray a short prayer to Saint Michael, asking him to defend them. Pope Leo XIII wrote that prayer in 1886.

Long ago, the Church kept a feast for Saint Michael on September 29. Since 1969, that day has honored all three archangels together. Saint Michael is a patron saint of soldiers and police officers, who work to keep others safe.

pages.intro: Saint Gabriel is an angel, a spirit created by God. In the Bible, God sends Gabriel to carry his most important messages. Gabriel told a priest named Zechariah that he would have a son, John the Baptist. Then Gabriel was sent to a young woman named Mary, in the town of Nazareth, to tell her that she would be the Mother of God's Son.
story_paragraphs: Saint Gabriel is not a person who lived on earth. He is an angel. Angels are spirits created by God. They serve God and carry his messages. Gabriel is one of only three angels named in the Bible.
The name Gabriel means "God is my strength."

Gabriel first appears in the Old Testament. A holy man named Daniel was praying when Gabriel came to him. The angel said, "Daniel, I have now come to give you understanding." He told Daniel that God had heard his prayer.

Many years later, God sent Gabriel to the Temple in Jerusalem. A priest named Zechariah was serving there. He and his wife Elizabeth were old and had no children. Gabriel told him they would have a son and should name him John. Zechariah could hardly believe it. The angel answered, "I am Gabriel, who stand before God. I was sent to speak to you and to announce to you this good news."
Six months later came Gabriel's greatest message. God sent him to a town in Galilee called Nazareth, to a young woman named Mary. Gabriel said to her, "Hail, favored one! The Lord is with you."

Mary was troubled and wondered what this greeting meant. The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God." He told her that she would have a son and name him Jesus, and that he would be called the Son of the Most High. Gabriel also said, "Nothing will be impossible for God."
Mary answered, "Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. May it be done to me according to your word." Then the angel left her.
This moment is called the Annunciation. Every time we pray the Hail Mary, we begin with the greeting Gabriel brought to Mary.

pages.intro: Saint Raphael is an angel, a spirit created by God. His name means "God heals." The Bible tells his story in the Book of Tobit. There, God sends Raphael to travel with a young man named Tobiah on a long and dangerous trip. Raphael looks like an ordinary traveler. Only at the end does the family learn that an angel has been with them all along.
story_paragraphs: Saint Raphael is an angel, not a person who lived on earth. He is one of only three angels named in the Bible. His story is told in the Old Testament, in the Book of Tobit.
Tobit was a good man who had become blind. Long before, he had left some money with a relative in a faraway land called Media. Now he needed it. He asked his son, Tobiah, to go and bring it back.

Tobiah needed someone to show him the way. He went out and found a young man who said he knew all the roads. The young man said his name was Azariah. Tobiah did not know it, but this was the angel Raphael.
So the two set out together, and Tobiah's dog followed along behind them.

One evening, Tobiah went down to wash his feet in the Tigris River. A large fish leaped out of the water at him! The angel called, "Grab the fish and hold on to it!" Tobiah pulled it up on the shore. Raphael told him to save some parts of the fish, because they could be used as medicine.
On the journey, Raphael also helped Tobiah meet and marry a young woman named Sarah, who had suffered many sorrows. With the angel's help, her troubles ended.

At last they came home. Raphael told Tobiah to put the medicine from the fish on his father's eyes. Tobiah did, and his father could see again. Tobit hugged his son and cried, "I can see you, son, the light of my eyes!"

Then the traveler told them the truth. "I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand and serve before the Glory of the Lord." Tobit and Tobiah fell to the ground in fear. But Raphael said, "Do not fear; peace be with you! Bless God now and forever." Then he returned to God.

pages.subtitle: Honored as the parents of Mary and the grandparents of Jesus.

quick_facts.label: Lived
quick_facts.value: Before the birth of Jesus

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Nazareth, according to tradition

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Being the parents of Mary and the grandparents of Jesus

pages.intro: Mary, the Mother of Jesus, had a mother and father who raised her to love God. Christians have called them Joachim and Anne for a very long time. The Bible does not tell us about them. Their names and their story come from a very old tradition. The Church honors them as the grandparents of Jesus and as patron saints of all grandparents.
story_paragraphs: Have you ever wondered who Jesus's grandparents were? Mary, his mother, had parents who cared for her and taught her to pray. The Church honors them as Saints Joachim and Anne.

The Bible does not tell us anything about Mary's parents. It does not even give their names. What we know comes from tradition. Their names and their story are found in a book written about 150 years after the time of Jesus. That book is not part of the Bible, and we cannot be sure the details happened just as it tells them.
Here is the story that has been handed down. Joachim and Anne lived in Nazareth. They loved God, but they had grown old without having any children, and this made them very sad.
Joachim went out into the countryside alone to pray. At home, Anne prayed too. She promised that if God gave her a child, she would give that child back to God to serve him.
Then an angel came to each of them with wonderful news. Anne would have a baby, and the child would be very special.

Joachim and Anne had a daughter, and they named her Mary. The story says that when Mary was three years old, her parents brought her to the Temple in Jerusalem to be raised there, just as Anne had promised.
Whatever the details were, one thing is certain. Mary had parents who loved her, and she grew up to say yes to God with her whole heart. That is why the Church honors Joachim and Anne.
Christians were building churches in honor of Saint Anne by the 500s. Today, Joachim and Anne share one feast day, July 26. They are the patron saints of grandparents.

pages.subtitle: A doctor and friend of Saint Paul who wrote down the story of Jesus with great care.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Antioch in Syria, according to tradition

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Writing the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles

pages.intro: Luke was a doctor who lived in the time of the apostles. He became a Christian and a faithful friend of Saint Paul. Luke wrote two books of the Bible: a Gospel about the life of Jesus, and the Acts of the Apostles, about the first Christians. Many of the stories we love best, like the Christmas story, come to us from Saint Luke.
story_paragraphs: Luke lived in the first century, the time of the apostles. He was a doctor. The Bible tells us this in a letter of Saint Paul, where Luke is described as a physician, which is another word for doctor.

Luke was not one of the twelve apostles, and he probably never met Jesus. An old tradition says he came from the city of Antioch, in Syria, and that he was not Jewish. He learned about Jesus from the first Christians.
Luke became a close friend and helper of Saint Paul. He stayed with Paul even in hard times. Near the end of Paul's life, when Paul was a prisoner, a letter says, "Luke is the only one with me."

Luke wanted people to know for certain what Jesus had said and done. So he talked with people who had been there from the beginning. He begins his Gospel by saying that he wrote it down "after investigating everything accurately anew," and that he put it "in an orderly sequence."

Luke's Gospel gives us stories that are not found in any of the others. Only Luke tells how the angel Gabriel came to Mary. Only Luke tells about the shepherds who visited the baby Jesus on the first Christmas. Two of the best-known stories Jesus told, the Good Samaritan and the Prodigal Son, are found only in Luke's Gospel too. Again and again, Luke shows how kind and forgiving God is.

Luke also wrote a second book, the Acts of the Apostles. It tells what happened after Jesus returned to heaven: how the Holy Spirit came, and how the apostles carried the Good News from Jerusalem all the way to Rome.

We do not know much about the rest of Luke's life. Because he was a doctor, he is the patron saint of doctors. An old story says he painted a picture of Mary, so he is the patron saint of artists as well.

pages.subtitle: A tax collector who got up and followed Jesus the moment he was called.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Galilee

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Leaving everything to follow Jesus; the first Gospel bears his name

pages.intro: Matthew was a tax collector. In his day, most people did not like tax collectors at all. One day, Jesus walked past the place where Matthew worked and said two words: "Follow me." Matthew got up and followed him. He became one of the twelve apostles. The first of the four Gospels in the Bible carries his name.
story_paragraphs: Matthew lived in Galilee in the time of Jesus. He had another name, too. The Gospels of Mark and Luke call him Levi.

Matthew's job was collecting taxes. Taxes are money that people must pay to their rulers. In those days, the land of Jesus was ruled by the Romans, and tax collectors gathered money for them. Many tax collectors also cheated and took extra for themselves. So most people did not like or trust them.
One day, Matthew was sitting at his work, at a place called the customs post. Jesus walked by and saw him. Jesus said, "Follow me." And Matthew got up and followed him. He left his old life behind.
Then there was a big dinner at the house, and Jesus came. Many other tax collectors and people known as sinners came too. They sat down to eat with Jesus and his disciples.
Some religious leaders, called Pharisees, saw this and did not like it. They asked the disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"

Jesus heard them. He said, "Those who are well do not need a physician, but the sick do." A physician is a doctor. Jesus meant that he had come to help the people who needed him most. He added, "I did not come to call the righteous but sinners."
Matthew became one of the twelve apostles. He was with Jesus as he taught and healed. After Jesus rose from the dead and returned to heaven, Matthew helped spread the Good News.

From early times, Christians have connected Matthew with the Gospel that comes first in the New Testament. It includes the Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus teaches the Our Father. We do not know for certain where Matthew went later or how he died. Different old stories tell it in different ways.

pages.subtitle: A young helper of the apostles who wrote down the story of Jesus.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Jerusalem

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Writing the Gospel of Mark

pages.intro: Mark was a young man in Jerusalem when the Church was just beginning. The first Christians met to pray in his mother's house. Mark traveled with Saint Paul and Saint Barnabas, and later he worked closely with Saint Peter. He wrote one of the four Gospels. It is the shortest Gospel, and many think it was the first one written.
story_paragraphs: Mark is also called John Mark in the Bible. He lived in Jerusalem with his mother, whose name was Mary. The first Christians often gathered in her house to pray.

One night, something amazing happened there. Saint Peter had been put in prison, and the Christians were praying for him at the house. An angel led Peter out of the prison, and he came straight to their door and knocked. A servant girl named Rhoda heard his voice. She was so happy that she forgot to open the gate! She ran inside to tell everyone, while Peter kept knocking.

As a young man, Mark went with Saint Paul and Saint Barnabas to help them on a missionary trip. But partway through the first journey, Mark turned back and went home. Later, Paul and Barnabas disagreed about whether to take him along again.

That was not the end of Mark's story. He kept serving, and the friendship was mended. Years later, when Paul was a prisoner, a letter asks, "Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is helpful to me in the ministry."
Mark was especially close to Saint Peter. In one of his letters, Peter calls him "Mark, my son."

A very early Christian writer said that Mark was Peter's helper and that he wrote down carefully what Peter taught about Jesus. That is how we have the Gospel of Mark. It is the shortest of the four Gospels. It moves quickly, and it shows how Jesus gave his life out of love for us.

An old tradition says that Mark later carried the Good News to Egypt and began the Church in the great city of Alexandria, and that he died there for his faith. Christians in Egypt still honor him as their first leader.

pages.subtitle: A fisherman who became one of Jesus's closest friends and took care of Mary.

quick_facts.label: Lived
quick_facts.fallback_value: the time of Jesus; died about the year 100

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Galilee, by the Sea of Galilee

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Being a close friend of Jesus and teaching that God is love

pages.intro: John was a fisherman. He and his brother James were mending their nets when Jesus called them, and they left everything to follow him. John became one of Jesus's closest friends. He stood by the cross when Jesus died, and Jesus asked him to take care of his mother, Mary. Christians honor John as the writer of the fourth Gospel.
story_paragraphs: John and his brother James were fishermen on the Sea of Galilee. Their father's name was Zebedee. One day, the two brothers were in a boat with their father, mending their nets. Jesus walked by and called them. Right away, they left their father in the boat and followed Jesus.
John became one of the twelve apostles. He, his brother James, and Peter were often the ones closest to Jesus at the most important moments.
The fourth Gospel speaks of "the disciple whom Jesus loved." From early times, Christians have believed that this disciple was John.

When Jesus was dying on the cross, most of his friends had run away. But that disciple was there, standing beside Mary, the Mother of Jesus. Jesus looked at his mother and said, "Woman, behold, your son." Then he said to the disciple, "Behold, your mother." From that hour, the disciple took Mary into his home and cared for her.

On Easter morning, Mary Magdalene came running with news that the tomb was open. Peter and the other disciple ran to see. The other disciple ran faster and got there first. He looked into the empty tomb, and he believed.
Later, some of the disciples were fishing when a man called to them from the shore. It was this disciple who knew him first and said, "It is the Lord."

After Jesus returned to heaven, John worked alongside Peter, preaching and healing. Tradition says that he later lived in the city of Ephesus and grew very old there. A story from the early Church says that when he was too old to preach, he would simply say, "Little children, love one another."
John is honored as the writer of the fourth Gospel, three letters, and the Book of Revelation. Tradition says he died peacefully around the year 100.
